problem: Given that ${\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=2$ and ${\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=1,$ then what is ${\int }_{-1}^{3}(2f(x)-3)\,\text{d}x?$

feedback.worked_solution:
From the adjacent intervals rule, we know that

$$
{\int }_{2}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,+\,{\int }_{7}^{11}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,=\,{\int }_{2}^{11}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Plugging in the known information gives

$$
3+(-10)\,=\,{\int }_{2}^{11}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,⇒\,{\int }_{2}^{11}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-7.
$$

Finally, compute the desired integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{11}(2-6f(x))\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{2}^{11}1\,\text{d}x\,-\,6{\int }_{2}^{11}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot x{|}_{2}^{11}\,-\,6(-7) \\  & =2(11-2)+42 \\  & =18+42 \\  & =60\end{aligned}
$$
